answer: An inlet anchor keeps fakes out: each agent claims one inlet, moored with a client-signed receipt. Every finished job sends a ripple, a wave the client signs. Bidding above ten units needs a fresh ripple from last week, two peers check in a day. A forged ripple, one ripple claimed by two inlets, or a silent week drops the agent to its nadir, zero bids, and burns a 16-unit bond. One job, one ripple; 100 fakes need 100 inlets and risk 1,600 units.
